critical_steps: All square-root factors are the displayed positive matrices.
The two representation spaces coincide because Q_i=P_i R with one invertible R.
The cross synthesis-analysis composition equals K exactly.
For J={1}, the two theorem sides differ by 48i at f=(1,i), up to conjugation convention.
Taking real parts makes the two cross terms equal identically.
integrity.proof_basis: Exact two-dimensional positive matrices chosen so that the two representation spaces coincide.
integrity.unproved_limits: No claim is made about unrelated later theorems or about the absence of nonindexed corrections.

scientific_limitations: The finding concerns Theorem 3.2 and does not reassess the later inequalities in the article.
The exact first-public day used here is the verified date of an author-uploaded public full text; the journal issue is from 2020 but an earlier exact online day was not established.
The real-part correction is universal; the original equality may still hold for special dual pairs whose relevant cross inner product is real.
An unindexed erratum or informal correction may contain the same observation.
title: A missing real part in a controlled \(K\)-\(g\)-dual identity
